explanations: merge() is shallow: when a layer has a `pricing` section, that whole object replaces the `pricing` built so far, so only the keys the file or environment actually set are left. A Lisbon file with just `{ pricing: { surgeCap: 3 } }` drops baseFareCents and the other rates, and validation then rejects the config. An env override inside a section wipes the file's and the defaults' values in that section the same way. The fix merges nested objects key by key (arrays and scalars still replace), so each layer overrides only the leaves it sets. Because it builds new objects, DEFAULTS is never shared or modified.
